data.name: Evy
data.gender_notes: Evy is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Evy was a goddess of life and the breath of life. She was also associated with the Greek goddess Aphrodite and represented love, beauty, and fertility. The name Evy carries the meaning “Life, breath” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Evy usually hope their child will grow to embody life, breath and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes new beginnings and the gift of life.
data.etymology: Evy belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Life, breath.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Evy total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_latin.name: Evy
in_latin.meaning: Originating from Greek name Εύη (Eúē), meaning 'good' or 'well-being'.
in_latin.long_meaning: Deriving from Greek root εὖ (eû), signifying excellence, happiness, or flourishing. In early Christian tradition, the name Eúē (Εὐή) was associated with virtue and moral excellence. The Latinized form, Evy, carries on this significance, reflecting the Christian values of goodness and well-being.

in_english.name: Evy
in_english.meaning: Originating from Greek name Εύη (Eúē), meaning 'good' or 'well-being'.
in_english.long_meaning: Evy is a Christian name with roots in ancient Greek, signifying goodness, happiness, or flourishing. The name is derived from the Greek root εὖ (eû), which conveys excellence, virtue, and moral excellence. In biblical context, the concept of εὖ (eû) is associated with God's goodness and provision (Genesis 1:31, Matthew 5:48). As a Christian name, Evy reflects the biblical values of living a virtuous and excellent life, pleasing God in all aspects (Colossians 1:10, 1 Thessalonians 4:7).

data.cultural_impact: The name "Evelyn" was popular in Europe during the medieval period and was often given to daughters. The name can also be found in books and literature, as in the novel "Evelyn Waugh's Brideshead Revisited."
data.spiritual_significance: Evelyn is derived from the name "Eve," the first woman created by God. It is a reminder of the creation story and the importance of women in the biblical narrative.
